## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## serena
CRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'.

## tokensave
tokensave is a code-graph MCP server. Start with tokensave_context for any code exploration task — it returns relevant symbols, relationships, and code snippets for a natural-language query. Use tokensave_search to find specific symbols by name. Discovery and analysis tools are read-only and safe to call in parallel. Edit and session-memory tools can mutate local project state and declare readOnlyHint=false. When a tool result contains a `tokensave_metrics:` line, report the savings to the user (e.g. 'TokenSave\'d ~N tokens').

[open] Issue #182: Pipeline: Two-pass transcription — fast model live, accurate model post-session
  Author: @sam-fakhreddine
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/gitrdunhq/Record-Suite/issues/182

  Description:
    ## User Story
    
    **As a** user who wants both instant live transcription AND maximum accuracy in the final transcript,
    **I want** THE RECORD to use a fast small model during the meeting and a high-accuracy large model for the final version,
    **so that** I see text immediately while recording and get the best possible transcript in my library.
    
    ## Context
    
    There is a fundamental tension between speed (small model, instant results, lower accuracy) and quality (large model, higher latency, better WER). Two-pass transcription resolves this:
    
    - **Live pass (small/base model):** Real-time display during the meeting. Optimized for speed.
    - **Archive pass (large-v3 model):** Post-session batch transcription. Optimized for accuracy. Replaces the live transcript in the library.
    
    The `TranscriptionEngine` protocol already supports multiple instances with different models. The event-driven pipeline makes this a wiring change, not an architectural change.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    1. Wire two `WhisperKitPlugin` instances: one with base model (live), one with large-v3 (archive)
    2. Live pass: runs during recording via streaming chunks (existing path)
    3. Archive pass: runs post-session on the full audio file (or compressed archive from #126)
    4. Archive transcript replaces live transcript in DuckDB, preserving live version as `transcript_draft`
    5. Warm model pool keeps both models loaded if memory permits; evicts base model first under pressure
    
    ## Acceptance Criteria
    
    - [ ] Live transcription uses base/small model with < 2s latency per chunk
    - [ ] Archive transcription uses large-v3 model, runs post-session
    - [ ] Archive transcript replaces live transcript in library view
    - [ ] Live transcript preserved as draft for debugging/comparison
    - [ ] If archive pass fails, live transcript is kept (no data loss)
    - [ ] On 8GB machines, only one model loads at a time (archive pass after live model unloaded)
    - [ ] On 16GB+ machines, both models can be warm simultaneously
    - [ ] WER improvement: archive pass measurably better than live pass (test on reference corpus)
    - [ ] User can disable archive pass in Settings ("Use live transcription as final" toggle)
    
    ## Blocked By
    
    - Event-driven pipeline architecture (need parallel transcription stages)
    - Warm model pool (need two models loaded, memory management)
    
    ## Unlocks
    
    - Best of both worlds: instant + accurate
    - Pro tier differentiator (free tier: live only, Pro: two-pass)

# THE RECORD

Local-first macOS meeting transcription app. Swift 6.2, Clean Architecture, TDD.

## Resume

Read `CURRENT_STATE.md` — it has the current epic, phase, and next action.

## Orchestration

This file is the conductor. Epics execute in dependency order:

```
COMPLETED                                    REMAINING
─────────                                    ─────────
Epic 1: Core Recording ─┐
Epic 1.5: Capture Fixes  ├──→ Epic 3.5: Parakeet + Telemetry (no UI)
Epic 3: Transcription    │
Epic 4: Diarization     ─┘──→ Epic 5: Menu Bar UI (needs desk)
Epic 2: Storage         ─┘──→ Epic 6: Summarization (MLX/GPU)
                              Epic 7: Streaming + Translation
                              Epic 8: THE RECORD Engine (MCP + NLP)
```

Each epic follows 5 phases: **REFINE** (SPEC) → **PLAN** (TASKS.md) → **PROPERTIES** (formal properties) → **ACT** (code) → **VALIDATE** (integration).
Human checkpoint after PLAN and before ACT. Within ACT, layers build sequentially: Domain → Business → Infrastructure → Presentation.

PROPERTIES.md (template at `docs/planning/PROPERTIES-TEMPLATE.md`) captures 11 property categories:
FUNCTIONAL, SAFETY, LIVENESS, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, RELIABILITY, CONCURRENCY, OBSERVABILITY, UX, DATA INTEGRITY, PRIVACY.
Each property drives test generation (RED briefs) and reviewer validation (traceability matrix).

## Skills (Progressive Disclosure)

Read the skill file when entering that phase. Don't load all skills upfront.

| Phase / Layer | Skill File to Read |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Full epic workflow | `.claude/skills/therecord-epic-executor/SKILL.md` |
| Domain types | `.claude/skills/therecord-domain-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Business actors | `.claude/skills/therecord-business-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Infrastructure | `.claude/skills/therecord-infrastructure-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Presentation | `.claude/skills/therecord-presentation-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Quality gate | `.claude/skills/therecord-integration-validator/SKILL.md` |
| Pre-merge bug hunt | `.claude/skills/therecord-bug-hunt/SKILL.md` |

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

**Before any rename swarm, run GitNexus impact analysis to get the complete caller map:**

```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "methodName", direction: "upstream", file_path: "path/to/file.swift", includeTests: true })
```

Pass the full `byDepth.1` list to each rename agent — no grepping, no missed call sites.

**After the swarm, reindex and verify zero orphans:**

```bash
node ~/.npm/_npx/32f98f05d98eef45/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
```

Then run:
```
gitnexus_cypher("MATCH (a)-[{type:'CALLS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'oldName' RETURN a.name, a.filePath")
```

Any remaining hits = confirmed orphaned calls. The DuckDB `.execute()` SQL calls are false positives — filter by `filePath NOT CONTAINS 'DuckDB'` if needed.

## Subagent Briefing

When spawning agents for parallel work, include in the prompt:
- The skill file path to read
- SPEC and PLAN file paths for the current epic
- `Swift 6.2 -strict-concurrency=complete`, file size limits, TDD discipline
- context7 MCP access: `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__query-docs`

## Canonical Decisions (override older docs)

Some architecture docs predate the SPEC-EPIC1 v2.0 research enrichment. When in conflict:
- **Audio capture:** ScreenCaptureKit (NOT CATapDescription). SPEC-EPIC1.md is authoritative.
- **Project name:** THE RECORD (not "Meeting Transcriber Pro"). Some planning docs use the old name.
- **Observation:** @Observable (NOT ObservableObject). macOS 15+ only.

## Single Source of Truth — Canonical Defaults

**Never hardcode a value that already has a named canonical source.** Reference the source directly so changes propagate automatically.

| Value | Canonical source | Wrong |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

## Deep Reference

Read `docs/architecture/swift-pitfalls.md` before Infrastructure or Presentation work
(actor re-entrancy, @unchecked Sendable, parallel test conflicts, diagnostic methodology).

These docs exist but don't read them unless working on that layer:
- `docs/architecture/DOMAIN-LAYER.md` (1681 lines)
- `docs/architecture/BUSINESS-LAYER.md` (1377 lines)
- `docs/architecture/INFRASTRUCTURE-LAYER.md` (1954 lines)
- `docs/architecture/PRESENTATION-LAYER.md` (2045 lines)
- `docs/architecture/PLUGIN-ARCHITECTURE.md` (2367 lines)
- `docs/planning/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md` (1239 lines)

## Git Commits

Format: `Epic {N}: [{Layer}] {Description}`

## Project Layout

```
Sources/Domain/          ← library: Foundation only
Sources/Business/        ← library: depends on Domain
Sources/Infrastructure/  ← library: depends on Domain + 3rd-party
Sources/Presentation/    ← library: depends on Domain + Business
Sources/THE RECORD/                ← executable: composition root (THE RECORDApp.swift)
Tests/Unit/{Domain,Business,Infrastructure,Presentation}/
Tests/{Integration,E2E}/
docs/epics/epic-{N}/{requirements,plan,validation,execution}/
```

# GitNexus — Code Intelligence

This project is indexed by GitNexus as **the-record** (5454 symbols, 52742 relationships, 239 execution flows). Use the GitNexus MCP tools to understand code, assess impact, and navigate safely.

> If any GitNexus tool warns the index is stale, run `npx gitnexus analyze` in terminal first.

## Always Do

- **MUST run impact analysis before editing any symbol.** Before modifying a function, class, or method, run `gitnexus_impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})` and report the blast radius (direct callers, affected processes, risk level) to the user.
- **MUST run `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before committing** to verify your changes only affect expected symbols and execution flows.
- **MUST warn the user** if impact analysis returns HIGH or CRITICAL risk before proceeding with edits.
- When exploring unfamiliar code, use `gitnexus_query({query: "concept"})` to find execution flows instead of grepping. It returns process-grouped results ranked by relevance.

- NEVER edit a function, class, or method without first running `gitnexus_impact` on it.
- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis.
- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `gitnexus_rename` which understands the call graph.

| Pre-merge bug hunt | `.claude/skills/therecord-bug-hunt/SKILL.md` |

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

**Before any rename swarm, run GitNexus impact analysis to get the complete caller map:**

```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "methodName", direction: "upstream", file_path: "path/to/file.swift", includeTests: true })
```

Pass the full `byDepth.1` list to each rename agent — no grepping, no missed call sites.

**After the swarm, reindex and verify zero orphans:**

```bash
node ~/.npm/_npx/32f98f05d98eef45/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
```

Then run:
```
gitnexus_cypher("MATCH (a)-[{type:'CALLS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'oldName' RETURN a.name, a.filePath")
```

Any remaining hits = confirmed orphaned calls. The DuckDB `.execute()` SQL calls are false positives — filter by `filePath NOT CONTAINS 'DuckDB'` if needed.

## Subagent Briefing

When spawning agents for parallel work, include in the prompt:
- The skill file path to read
- SPEC and PLAN file paths for the current epic
- `Swift 6.2 -strict-concurrency=complete`, file size limits, TDD discipline
- context7 MCP access: `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__query-docs`

## Canonical Decisions (override older docs)

Some architecture docs predate the SPEC-EPIC1 v2.0 research enrichment. When in conflict:
- **Audio capture:** ScreenCaptureKit (NOT CATapDescription). SPEC-EPIC1.md is authoritative.
- **Project name:** THE RECORD (not "Meeting Transcriber Pro"). Some planning docs use the old name.
- **Observation:** @Observable (NOT ObservableObject). macOS 15+ only.

## Single Source of Truth — Canonical Defaults

**Never hardcode a value that already has a named canonical source.** Reference the source directly so changes propagate automatically.

| Value | Canonical source | Wrong |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh pr create --repo gitrdunhq/Record-Suite --title "Epic 182: Two-pass transcription — fast model live, accurate model archive" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Closes #182.

Wires two-pass transcription into the pipeline: a fast base model runs during recording for live display, and a high-accuracy large-v3 model runs post-session (the archive pass) to replace the live transcript in the library. Draft is preserved for debugging.

- **Domain**: `TranscriptionConfig.archivePassEnabled` flag; `TranscriptRepository` split into `TranscriptReadRepository` / `TranscriptWriteRepository` protocols; `TranscriptionEngine.unloadModel()` for memory gate
- **Business**: `PipelineCoordinator` — archive pass gate (`archivePassEnabled`), memory gate (unloads primary engine below 12 GB), `recoverPendingSession` guard; `CleanupTranscriptionUseCase` — preserves live transcript as draft before archive pass
- **Infrastructure**: `DuckDBWriterActor.saveDraftTranscript`, `DuckDBSQL` migration for `transcript_draft` column, `DuckDBReaderActor+Transcript`
- **Presentation**: `TranscriptionSubAssembler` exposes `primaryEngine` and `transcriptReader`; `AppAssembler` / `AppAssemblerBuilders` wire `archivePassEnabled` reactively from settings
- **Tests**: 55 new tests — archive pass gate, memory gate (8 GB / 12 GB / 16 GB), draft preservation, settings toggle, streaming contract
- **Pre-existing fixes**: swiftlint excludes for datum worktrees (cleared 103 `for_where` + 212 `cyclomatic_complexity` noise); accessibility labels on `MenuBarPopover`, `SettingsViewDeleteAllSection`, `BroadsheetRootView`; `.gitignore` for AI tool configs and scratch dirs

## Test plan

- [ ] `swift test` — 939/939 passing locally
- [ ] Archive pass gate: `startCleanupPass` runs when `archivePassEnabled=true`, skips when false
- [ ] Memory gate: `unloadModel` called on 8 GB machines, skipped on 12 GB+
- [ ] Draft preservation: live transcript saved as `transcript_draft` before archive pass overwrites
- [ ] Settings toggle: "Use live transcription as final" disables archive pass reactively
- [ ] If archive pass fails, live transcript is kept (no data loss)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code)
EOF
)"

Execution mode rules:
- If the raw arguments include `--wait`, do not ask. Run in the foreground.
- If the raw arguments include `--background`, do not ask. Run in a Claude background task.
- Otherwise, estimate the review size before asking:

2	/// dependency on WhisperKit, CoreML, or any other inference framework.
3	///
4	/// Conforming types are expected to be actors or otherwise internally
5	/// thread-safe; the `Sendable` requirement enforces that instances can cross
6	/// concurrency boundaries without data races under Swift strict concurrency.
7	public protocol TranscriptionEngine: Sendable {
8	    // MARK: - Lifecycle
9	
10	    /// Loads and prepares the model identified by `modelId` for inference.
11	    ///
12	    /// Must be called before ``transcribe(samples:context:)``.
13	    /// Implementations should be idempotent: calling this with the same
14	    /// `modelId` when the model is already loaded is a no-op.
15	    ///
16	    /// - Parameter modelId: The typed model identifier.
17	    /// - Throws: A domain error if the model cannot be found or loaded.
18	    func loadModel(_ modelId: ModelID) async throws
19	
20	    // MARK: - Inference
21	
22	    /// Transcribes a buffer of PCM audio samples.
23	    ///
24	    /// - Parameters:
25	    ///   - samples: Mono, 16 kHz, 32-bit float PCM samples.
26	    ///   - context: Metadata that guides engine behaviour for this chunk.
27	    /// - Returns: A ``TranscriptionSegment`` representing the recognised speech.
28	    /// - Throws: A domain error if transcription fails or the engine is not ready.
29	    func transcribe(
30	        samples: [Float],
31	        context: TranscriptionContext
32	    ) async throws -> TranscriptionSegment

36	    ///
37	    /// The default implementation delegates to ``transcribe(samples:context:)``
38	    /// and wraps the result in a single-element array, preserving backward

41	    /// Override this method when the underlying engine produces time-aligned

46	    // MARK: - Execute
47	
48	    /// Runs the cleanup transcription pass for a stored recording.
49	    ///
50	    /// - Parameters:
51	    ///   - recordingId: Unique identifier of the stored recording to transcribe.
52	    ///   - modelId: Identifier of the higher-quality model to use for
53	    ///     the cleanup pass (e.g. `"openai_whisper-base.en"`).
54	    /// - Returns: A ``TranscriptionResult`` with ``TranscriptionPassType/cleanup``
55	    ///   containing the refined transcript.
56	    /// - Throws: Any error produced by the storage, sample loader, or
57	    ///   transcription engine — errors are never swallowed here.
58	    // sequential setup — extraction would harm readability
59	    // swiftlint:disable:next function_body_length
60	    public func transcribeCleanupPass(
61	        recordingId: RecordingID,
62	        modelId: ModelID,
63	    ) async throws -> TranscriptionResult {
64	        logger
65	            .info(
66	                // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
67	                "Starting cleanup pass for recording \(recordingId, privacy: .private) with model \(modelId, privacy: .public)",
68	            )
69	
70	        let signposter = AppLogger.signposter(category: "Performance")
71	        let signpostState = signposter.beginInterval("Pipeline Cleanup", id: signposter.makeSignpostID())
72	        defer { signposter.endInterval("Pipeline Cleanup", signpostState) }
73	
74	        // Fetch recording metadata from repository.
75	        // We do not require an active lock or check `isTranscribing`
76	        // here because cleanup handles orphaned or broken transcriptions.
77	        let recording = try await reader.getRecording(id: recordingId)
78	        logger.info("Retrieved recording: \(recording.metadata.id, privacy: .public)")
79	
80	        // 2. Extract the audio file URL from the recording metadata.
81	        let audioURL = recording.metadata.audioURL
82	
83	        // 3. Load PCM samples and the cleanup model in parallel.
84	        // checkCancellation between the two async let declarations is intentional:
85	        // structured concurrency will cancel the started `samples` task on scope exit
86	        // if this throws, so we can safely start both operations.
87	        async let samples = sampleLoader.loadSamples(from: audioURL)
88	        try Task.checkCancellation()
89	        async let modelLoad: Void = transcription.loadModel(modelId)
90	        let (loadedSamples, _) = try await (samples, modelLoad)
91	        logger
92	            .info(
93	                // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
94	                "Loaded \(loadedSamples.count, privacy: .public) PCM samples from \(audioURL.lastPathComponent, privacy: .public)",
95	            )
96	        logger.info("Model loaded: \(modelId, privacy: .public)")
97	
98	        // 4. Build the transcription context for a full-file cleanup pass.
99	        let context = TranscriptionContext(
100	            modelId: modelId,
101	            isFinalChunk: true,
102	        )
103	
104	        // 5. Transcribe — time the inference for result metadata.
105	        let startTime = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent()
106	        try Task.checkCancellation()
107	        let segments = try await transcription.transcribeSegments(samples: loadedSamples, context: context)
108	        let computeUnit = await transcription.getComputeUnit()
109	        let elapsed = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - startTime
110	
111	        logger
112	            .info(
113	                // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
114	                "Cleanup transcription complete in \(elapsed, format: .fixed(precision: 3), privacy: .public)s — \(segments.count, privacy: .public) segments",
115	            )
116	
117	        // 5b. Record inference telemetry.
118	        let audioDuration = Double(loadedSamples.count) / 16000.0
119	        let avgConfidence = segments.isEmpty ? 0.0 : segments.map(\.confidence).reduce(0, +) / Double(segments.count)
120	        await telemetry?.record(InferenceMetrics(
121	            modelId: modelId,
122	            audioDuration: audioDuration,
123	            inferenceDuration: elapsed,
124	            realTimeFactor: elapsed > 0 ? audioDuration / elapsed : 0,
125	            confidence: avgConfidence,
126	            sampleCount: loadedSamples.count,
127	            computeUnit: computeUnit,
128	            timestamp: Date(),
129	        ))
130	
131	        // 6. Build the TranscriptionResult with passType .cleanup.
132	        let fullText = segments.map(\.text).joined(separator: " ")
133	        let result = TranscriptionResult(
134	            segments: segments,
135	            fullText: fullText,
136	            processingTime: elapsed,
137	            modelId: modelId,
138	            recordedAt: recording.metadata.recordedAt,
139	            computeUnit: computeUnit,
140	            passType: .cleanup,
141	        )
142	
143	        // Save draft of the original live transcript before overwriting (idempotent guard).
144	        // Skipped when no transcriptReader is injected (can't verify idempotency without it).
145	        if let transcriptReader {
146	            let existingDraft = try await transcriptReader.getTranscriptDraft(for: recordingId)
147	            if existingDraft == nil, let liveText = recording.transcript?.fullText, !liveText.isEmpty {
148	                try await writer.saveDraftTranscript(draftText: liveText, for: recordingId)
149	            }
150	        }
151	
152	        // Update database with final cleaned transcript.
153	        logger.info("Saving cleaned transcript for \(recordingId.rawValue, privacy: .public)")
154	        try await writer.updateTranscript(id: recordingId, transcript: result)
155	
156	        return result
157	    }
158	}

2	import FluidAudio
3	import Foundation
4	import Logging
5	import Utilities
6	
7	// MARK: - ParakeetPlugin
8	
9	/// FluidAudio/Parakeet TDT transcription engine (Apple Silicon optimised).
10	///
11	/// ## Thread Safety
12	/// All mutable state (`asrManager`, `loadedModelId`, `sequenceCounter`) is
13	/// actor-isolated. `AsrManager` is itself an actor; all calls to it cross
14	/// isolation boundaries via `await`.
15	///
16	/// ## Decoder State
17	/// A fresh `TdtDecoderState` is created per `transcribe` call, making each
18	/// invocation stateless. This is appropriate for batch/chunk processing where
19	/// the caller manages session continuity via `TranscriptionContext`.
20	///
21	/// ## warm-up
22	/// `warmUp()` is a no-op: `AsrManager` prewarms its CoreML models during
23	/// `initialize` / `loadModels`. No additional pass is needed.
24	public actor ParakeetPlugin: TranscriptionEngine {
25	    // MARK: - Actor State
26	
27	    private var asrManager: AsrManager?
28	    private var loadedModelId: ModelID?
29	    private var sequenceCounter = 0
30	    public private(set) var downloadDelegate: (any ModelDownloadDelegate)?
31	
32	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "Parakeet")
33	
34	    // MARK: - Init
35	
36	    public init() {}
37	
38	    public func setDownloadDelegate(_ delegate: (any ModelDownloadDelegate)?) {
39	        downloadDelegate = delegate
40	    }
41	
42	    // MARK: - TranscriptionEngine
43	
44	    public func loadModel(_ modelId: ModelID) async throws {
45	        if loadedModelId == modelId, asrManager != nil {
46	            logger.info("Parakeet model already loaded — skipping")
47	            return
48	        }
49	
50	        logger.info("Loading Parakeet model '\(modelId, privacy: .public)'")
51	        await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(
52	            .init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 0.0, phase: .downloading)
53	        )
54	
55	        do {
56	            let models = try await withTimeout(TimeoutConfig.modelLoad) {
57	                try await AsrModels.downloadAndLoad(version: .v3)
58	            }
59	
60	            await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(
61	                .init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 0.6, phase: .compiling)
62	            )
63	
64	            let tdtConfig = TdtConfig(blankId: AsrModelVersion.v3.blankId)
65	            let asrConfig = ASRConfig(
66	                tdtConfig: tdtConfig,
67	                encoderHiddenSize: AsrModelVersion.v3.encoderHiddenSize
68	            )
69	            let manager = AsrManager(config: asrConfig)
70	            try await manager.loadModels(models)
71	
72	            asrManager = manager
73	            loadedModelId = modelId
74	
75	            await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(
76	                .init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 1.0, phase: .ready)
77	            )
78	            logger.info("Parakeet model '\(modelId, privacy: .public)' loaded")
79	        } catch {
80	            asrManager = nil
81	            loadedModelId = nil
82	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
83	            logger.error("Parakeet load error: \(errDesc, privacy: .private)")
84	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: error)
85	        }
86	    }
87	
88	    public func transcribe(
89	        samples: [Float],
90	        context: TranscriptionContext
91	    ) async throws -> Domain.TranscriptionSegment {
92	        guard !samples.isEmpty else {
93	            throw TranscriptionError.audioTooShort
94	        }
95	        guard let manager = asrManager else {
96	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: nil)
97	        }
98	
99	        let sid = context.sessionId?.rawValue ?? "none"
100	        // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
101	        logger.debug("Parakeet transcribing \(samples.count, privacy: .public) samples | session: \(sid, privacy: .private)")
102	
103	        let result: ASRResult
104	        let profiler = HardwareBoundaryProfiler(category: "Performance")
105	        let token = await profiler.begin("Parakeet Inference")
106	
107	        do {
108	            let layers = await manager.decoderLayerCount
109	            var decoderState = TdtDecoderState.make(decoderLayers: layers)
110	            result = try await manager.transcribe(samples, decoderState: &decoderState)
111	            await profiler.end(token)
112	        } catch {
113	            await profiler.end(token)
114	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
115	            logger.error("Parakeet inference error: \(errDesc, privacy: .private)")
116	            throw TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
117	        }
118	
119	        let seqNum = sequenceCounter
120	        sequenceCounter += 1
121	        return buildSegment(result: result, context: context, sequenceNumber: seqNum)
122	    }
123	
124	    public func isReady() async -> Bool {
125	        asrManager != nil
126	    }
127	
128	    /// No-op: Parakeet models are warm after `AsrManager.loadModels(_:)`.
129	    public func warmUp() async throws {}
130	
131	    // MARK: - Private Helpers
132	
133	    private func buildSegment(
134	        result: ASRResult,
135	        context: TranscriptionContext,
136	        sequenceNumber: Int
137	    ) -> Domain.TranscriptionSegment {
138	        let startTime = context.timestampOffset
139	        let endTime = startTime + result.duration
140	        let confidence = min(1.0, max(0.0, Double(result.confidence)))
141	
142	        return Domain.TranscriptionSegment(
143	            id: .generate(),
144	            text: result.text,
145	            startTime: startTime,
146	            endTime: endTime,
147	            confidence: confidence,
148	            isFinal: context.isFinalChunk,
149	            sequenceNumber: sequenceNumber
150	        )
151	    }
152	}

21	        let isTest = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil

47	                )

67	                do { try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 10_000_000_000) } catch {}
68	                // Application will terminate from the alert, so we just return dummy instances or exit safely
69	                exit(1)

73	        // DuckDB is single-writer-per-file. Each actor owns an independent file:
74	        //   therecord.duckdb     → DuckDBStorageActor   (recordings + segments)
75	        //   commitments.duckdb → DuckDBCommitmentStore (commitments)
76	        let commitmentStore: DuckDBCommitmentStore?

99	    /// Shows a fatal database-error alert, activates an existing instance if found,
100	    /// and terminates the app. Extracted to deduplicate the two identical alert blocks
101	    /// in `buildStorage`.
102	    @MainActor
103	    private func showFatalAlert(error: any Error) {

121	    func buildEngine(
122	        config: AppConfig,
123	        fallbackTrack: TrackCommitmentsUseCase,
124	        alignment: (any AlignmentUseCase)? = nil,

141	    func buildMCPProviders(config: AppConfig) -> [any ContextProvider] {
142	        guard config.mcpConsentGranted else { return [] }
143	
144	        // Try to create a context cache for semantic caching of query results.
145	        // If cache initialization fails, providers will work without caching.
146	        let contextCache: DuckDBContextCache?
147	        do {
148	            contextCache = try DuckDBContextCache(databasePath: nil)
149	        } catch {
150	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
151	            logger.warning("Failed to initialize context cache: \(errDesc, privacy: .public)")
152	            contextCache = nil
153	        }
154	
155	        // Migrate Keychain accessibility for existing credentials (no-op on clean install).
156	        let credentialStore = KeychainCredentialStore()
157	        try? credentialStore.migrateAccessibilityIfNeeded()
158	
159	        var providers: [any ContextProvider] = []
160	
161	        // Generic MCP endpoint providers (configured via mcpEndpoints).
162	        for endpoint in config.mcpEndpoints {
163	            let isLocal = endpoint.url.host == "localhost" || endpoint.url.host == "127.0.0.1"
164	            guard endpoint.url.scheme == "https" || isLocal else { continue }
165	            let provider = GenericMCPProvider(endpoint: endpoint.url, providerID: endpoint.providerID)
166	            providers.append(provider)
167	        }
168	
169	        // Notion provider: constructed when the user has enabled the Notion integration.
170	        if config.notionEnabled {
171	            providers.append(NotionProvider(credentialStore: credentialStore))
172	        }
173	
174	        // Obsidian provider: constructed when the user has configured a vault path.
175	        if let vaultPath = config.obsidianVaultPath, !vaultPath.isEmpty {
176	            providers.append(ObsidianProvider(vaultPath: URL(fileURLWithPath: vaultPath)))
177	        }

179	        // Wrap every provider in the caching layer when a cache is available.
180	        guard let cache = contextCache else { return providers }
181	        let cacheConfig = config.contextCache
182	        return providers.map { provider in
183	            CachingContextProvider(
184	                inner: provider,
185	                cache: cache,
186	                ttlSeconds: cacheConfig.exactTTLSeconds,
187	                semanticTTLSeconds: cacheConfig.semanticTTLSeconds,

content.text:
Two options:

**`tsx` (fastest, no config needed)**
```bash
npx tsx script.ts
# or install globally:
npm install -g tsx
tsx script.ts
```

**`ts-node`**
```bash
npx ts-node script.ts
# or globally:
npm install -g ts-node
ts-node script.ts
```

`tsx` is the move — it's faster, handles ESM/CJS transparently, and needs zero config. `ts-node` is older and sometimes needs a `tsconfig.json` to behave.

# TheRecord Release Builder

## Your Responsibility

Run the release build pipeline and report the DMG path. One script, one output.

---

## Steps

### 0. Check for uncommitted changes

Before building, run:

```bash
wfc git status
```

If there are uncommitted changes, **stop and ask the user** — the DMG SHA is derived from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, so uncommitted work won't be reflected in the build ID. The right question to ask: "You have uncommitted changes — want me to commit them first so they're in the build ID, or release from the current commit?"

Only proceed once the user has confirmed or committed.

### 1. Run the release script

```bash
bash scripts/release.sh --clean --open 2>&1
```

Always pass `--clean`. The script handles everything:
- `swift package clean` — wipes the build cache so no stale artifacts sneak in
- `swift build -c release`
- `.app` bundle assembly with `Info.plist` + entitlements
- Ad-hoc codesigning (uses "TheRecord Dev" identity if present, falls back to `-`)
- DMG creation via `hdiutil`
- Cleanup of DMGs older than the 5 most recent

Other flags:
- `--skip-build` — reuse an existing binary (skip compile + clean), useful for re-signing or re-packaging
- `--open` — open the DMG immediately after creation

### 2. Report the result

When the script succeeds, extract and show the user:
- DMG path (`.build/release/TheRecord-{VERSION}-{SHA}.dmg`)
- DMG size
- One-liner to open it: `open .build/release/TheRecord-*.dmg`

### 3. On failure, diagnose

| Error | Likely cause | Fix |
|-------|-------------|-----|
| `Binary not found` | `swift build -c release` failed | Re-run `swift build -c release 2>&1` and fix compiler errors first |
| `codesign: error` | No signing identity | Acceptable — ad-hoc fallback is used automatically |
| `hdiutil: create failed` | Disk full or bad tmp dir | `df -h .build/` to check space |
| `Permission denied` | Script not executable | `chmod +x scripts/release.sh` |

---

## What NOT to do

- Do not run `swift build` manually before the script — the script does it
- Do not commit the DMG or `.build/` — both are gitignored
- Do not use `xcodebuild` — this is a pure SwiftPM project

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# release.sh — Build a signed release DMG for BodyMan.
# Usage: bash scripts/release.sh [--skip-build] [--open]
set -euo pipefail

APP_NAME="BodyMan"
BUNDLE_ID="com.bodyman.app"
VERSION="1.5.0"
BUILD_SHA=$(wfc git rev-parse --short)
BUILD_DIR="$(swift build -c release --show-bin-path 2>/dev/null || echo '.build/release')"
APP_BUNDLE="$BUILD_DIR/$APP_NAME.app"
DMG_NAME="$APP_NAME-$VERSION-$BUILD_SHA.dmg"
DMG_PATH="$BUILD_DIR/$DMG_NAME"
SKIP_BUILD=false
OPEN_AFTER=false
CLEAN_BUILD=false

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --skip-build) SKIP_BUILD=true ;;
        --open)       OPEN_AFTER=true ;;
        --clean)      CLEAN_BUILD=true ;;
    esac
done

echo "=== BodyMan Release $VERSION ($BUILD_SHA) ==="

# 1. Compile
if [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = true ]; then
    echo "[1/5] Skipping compile (--skip-build)"
else
    if [ "$CLEAN_BUILD" = true ]; then
        echo "[1/5] Cleaning build artifacts..."
        swift package clean
    fi
    echo "[1/5] Compiling release build..."
    swift build -c release
fi

BINARY="$BUILD_DIR/$APP_NAME"
if [ ! -f "$BINARY" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Binary not found at $BINARY — run without --skip-build"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# release.sh — Build a signed release DMG for BodyMan.
# Usage: bash scripts/release.sh [--skip-build] [--open]
set -euo pipefail

APP_NAME="BodyMan"
BUNDLE_ID="com.bodyman.app"
VERSION="1.5.0"
BUILD_SHA=$(wfc git rev-parse --short)
BUILD_DIR="$(swift build -c release --show-bin-path 2>/dev/null || echo '.build/release')"
APP_BUNDLE="$BUILD_DIR/$APP_NAME.app"
DMG_NAME="$APP_NAME-$VERSION-$BUILD_SHA.dmg"
DMG_PATH="$BUILD_DIR/$DMG_NAME"
SKIP_BUILD=false
OPEN_AFTER=false
CLEAN_BUILD=false

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --skip-build) SKIP_BUILD=true ;;
        --open)       OPEN_AFTER=true ;;
        --clean)      CLEAN_BUILD=true ;;
    esac
done

echo "=== BodyMan Release $VERSION ($BUILD_SHA) ==="

# 1. Compile
if [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = true ]; then
    echo "[1/5] Skipping compile (--skip-build)"
else
    if [ "$CLEAN_BUILD" = true ]; then
        echo "[1/5] Cleaning build artifacts..."
        swift package clean
    fi
    echo "[1/5] Compiling release build..."
    swift build -c release
fi

BINARY="$BUILD_DIR/$APP_NAME"
if [ ! -f "$BINARY" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Binary not found at $BINARY — run without --skip-build"
    exit 1
fi

# 2. Assemble .app bundle
echo "[2/5] Assembling app bundle..."
rm -rf "$APP_BUNDLE"
mkdir -p "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/MacOS"
mkdir -p "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Resources"
cp "$BINARY" "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/MacOS/$APP_NAME"

cat > "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Info.plist" << PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleDevelopmentRegion</key><string>en</string>
    <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>BodyMan</string>
    <key>CFBundleIconFile</key><string>AppIcon</string>
    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>$BUNDLE_ID</string>
    <key>CFBundleInfoDictionaryVersion</key><string>6.0</string>
    <key>CFBundleName</key><string>BodyMan</string>
    <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key><string>BodyMan</string>
    <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
    <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>$VERSION</string>
    <key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>$BUILD_SHA</string>
    <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>26.0</string>
    <key>NSPrincipalClass</key><string>NSApplication</string>
    <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key><true/>
    <key>LSUIElement</key><false/>
    <key>NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription</key>
    <string>BodyMan reads your calendar to detect upcoming meetings and show attendee context.</string>
    <key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
    <string>BodyMan uses the microphone to capture meeting audio for transcription.</string>
    <key>NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription</key>
    <string>BodyMan captures meeting audio for transcription.</string>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST

# 3. Codesign
echo "[3/5] Codesigning..."
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR/tmp"
ENTITLEMENTS="$BUILD_DIR/tmp/bodyman-entitlements.plist"
cat > "$ENTITLEMENTS" << 'ENT'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>com.apple.security.app-sandbox</key><false/>
    <key>com.apple.security.personal-information.calendars</key><true/>
    <key>com.apple.security.device.audio-input</key><true/>
    <key>com.apple.security.device.camera</key><true/>
</dict>
</plist>
ENT

SIGN_IDENTITY="BodyMan Dev"
if security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$SIGN_IDENTITY"; then
    codesign --force --sign "$SIGN_IDENTITY" --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --deep "$APP_BUNDLE"
    echo "    Signed with: $SIGN_IDENTITY"
else
    codesign --force --sign - --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --deep "$APP_BUNDLE"
    echo "    Signed ad-hoc (no '$SIGN_IDENTITY' identity found)"
fi
rm -f "$ENTITLEMENTS"

# 4. Verify
echo "[4/5] Verifying..."
codesign --verify --verbose "$APP_BUNDLE" 2>&1 || echo "    Warning: verification issue (expected for ad-hoc)"

# 5. Create DMG
echo "[5/5] Creating DMG..."
rm -f "$DMG_PATH"
DMG_TMP="$BUILD_DIR/tmp/dmg-staging"
rm -rf "$DMG_TMP"
mkdir -p "$DMG_TMP"
cp -R "$APP_BUNDLE" "$DMG_TMP/"
ln -s /Applications "$DMG_TMP/Applications"
hdiutil create -volname "$APP_NAME" -srcfolder "$DMG_TMP" -ov -format UDZO "$DMG_PATH" 2>&1 | tail -2
rm -rf "$DMG_TMP"

# Cleanup: keep only the 5 most recent DMGs
OLD_DMGS=$(ls -t "$BUILD_DIR"/*.dmg 2>/dev/null | tail -n +6)
if [ -n "$OLD_DMGS" ]; then
    echo "Cleaning up old DMGs..."
    echo "$OLD_DMGS" | xargs rm -f
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Done ==="
echo "App:  $APP_BUNDLE"
echo "DMG:  $DMG_PATH"
echo "Size: $(du -sh "$DMG_PATH" | cut -f1)"
echo ""
echo "Install: open $DMG_PATH"

if [ "$OPEN_AFTER" = true ]; then
    open "$DMG_PATH"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# release.sh — Build a signed release DMG for THE RECORD.
# Usage: bash scripts/release.sh [--skip-build] [--open] [--clean]
set -euo pipefail

APP_NAME="THE RECORD"
BINARY_NAME="TheRecord"
BUNDLE_ID="app.the-record"
VERSION="0.9.0"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
BUILD_SHA=$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD)
BUILD_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.build/arm64-apple-macosx/release"
APP_BUNDLE="$BUILD_DIR/$BINARY_NAME.app"
DMG_NAME="TheRecord-$VERSION-$BUILD_SHA.dmg"
DMG_PATH="$BUILD_DIR/$DMG_NAME"
SKIP_BUILD=false
OPEN_AFTER=false
CLEAN_BUILD=false

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --skip-build) SKIP_BUILD=true ;;
        --open)       OPEN_AFTER=true ;;
        --clean)      CLEAN_BUILD=true ;;
    esac
done

echo "=== THE RECORD Release $VERSION ($BUILD_SHA) ==="

# 1. Compile
if [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = true ]; then
    echo "[1/5] Skipping compile (--skip-build)"
else
    if [ "$CLEAN_BUILD" = true ]; then
        echo "[1/5] Cleaning build artifacts..."
        swift package --package-path "$REPO_ROOT" clean
    fi
    echo "[1/5] Compiling release build..."
    swift build -c release --product TheRecord --package-path "$REPO_ROOT"
fi

BINARY="$BUILD_DIR/$BINARY_NAME"
if [ ! -f "$BINARY" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Binary not found at $BINARY — run without --skip-build"
    exit 1
fi

# 2. Assemble .app bundle
echo "[2/5] Assembling app bundle..."
rm -rf "$APP_BUNDLE"
mkdir -p "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/MacOS"
mkdir -p "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Resources"
cp "$BINARY" "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/MacOS/$BINARY_NAME"

PLIST_SRC="$REPO_ROOT/Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/Info.plist"
if [ -f "$PLIST_SRC" ]; then
    cp "$PLIST_SRC" "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Info.plist"
else
cat > "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Info.plist" << PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleDevelopmentRegion</key><string>en</string>
    <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>$BINARY_NAME</string>
    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>$BUNDLE_ID</string>
    <key>CFBundleInfoDictionaryVersion</key><string>6.0</string>
    <key>CFBundleName</key><string>THE RECORD</string>
    <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key><string>THE RECORD</string>
    <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
    <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>$VERSION</string>
    <key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>$BUILD_SHA</string>
    <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>15.0</string>
    <key>NSPrincipalClass</key><string>NSApplication</string>
    <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key><true/>
    <key>NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription</key>
    <string>THE RECORD reads your calendar to detect upcoming meetings and show attendee context.</string>
    <key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
    <string>THE RECORD records meeting audio for transcription.</string>
    <key>NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription</key>
    <string>THE RECORD captures meeting audio for transcription.</string>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST
fi

# 3. Codesign
echo "[3/5] Codesigning..."
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR/tmp"
ENTITLEMENTS="$BUILD_DIR/tmp/therecord-entitlements.plist"
cat > "$ENTITLEMENTS" << 'ENT'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>com.apple.security.app-sandbox</key><false/>
    <key>com.apple.security.personal-information.calendars</key><true/>
    <key>com.apple.security.device.audio-input</key><true/>
    <key>com.apple.security.device.camera</key><true/>
</dict>
</plist>
ENT

SIGN_IDENTITY="TheRecord Dev"
if security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$SIGN_IDENTITY"; then
    codesign --force --sign "$SIGN_IDENTITY" --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --deep "$APP_BUNDLE"
    echo "    Signed with: $SIGN_IDENTITY"
else
    codesign --force --sign - --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --deep "$APP_BUNDLE"
    echo "    Signed ad-hoc (no '$SIGN_IDENTITY' identity found)"
fi
rm -f "$ENTITLEMENTS"

# 4. Verify
echo "[4/5] Verifying..."
codesign --verify --verbose "$APP_BUNDLE" 2>&1 || echo "    Warning: verification issue (expected for ad-hoc)"

# 5. Create DMG
echo "[5/5] Creating DMG..."
rm -f "$DMG_PATH"
DMG_TMP="$BUILD_DIR/tmp/dmg-staging"
rm -rf "$DMG_TMP"
mkdir -p "$DMG_TMP"
cp -R "$APP_BUNDLE" "$DMG_TMP/"
ln -s /Applications "$DMG_TMP/Applications"
hdiutil create -volname "THE RECORD" -srcfolder "$DMG_TMP" -ov -format UDZO "$DMG_PATH" 2>&1 | tail -2
rm -rf "$DMG_TMP"

# Cleanup: keep only the 5 most recent DMGs
OLD_DMGS=$(ls -t "$BUILD_DIR"/TheRecord-*.dmg 2>/dev/null | tail -n +6)
if [ -n "$OLD_DMGS" ]; then
    echo "Cleaning up old DMGs..."
    echo "$OLD_DMGS" | xargs rm -f
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Done ==="
echo "App:  $APP_BUNDLE"
echo "DMG:  $DMG_PATH"
echo "Size: $(du -sh "$DMG_PATH" | cut -f1)"
echo ""
echo "Install: open $DMG_PATH"

if [ "$OPEN_AFTER" = true ]; then
    open "$DMG_PATH"
fi

// swift-tools-version:6.2
import PackageDescription

let debugWarningFlags: [SwiftSetting] = [
    .unsafeFlags(
        [
            "-Xfrontend", "-warn-long-function-bodies=100",
            "-Xfrontend", "-warn-long-expression-type-checking=100",
        ],
        .when(configuration: .debug),
    ),
]

let sharedSwiftSettings: [SwiftSetting] = [
    .enableExperimentalFeature("StrictConcurrency"),
    .unsafeFlags(["-strict-concurrency=complete"]),
] + debugWarningFlags

let package = Package(
    name: "TheRecord",
    platforms: [
        .macOS(.v15),
    ],
    products: [
        .executable(name: "TheRecord", targets: ["TheRecord"]),
        .library(name: "Business", targets: ["Business"]),
    ],
    dependencies: [
        .package(path: "../Record-Foundation"),
        .package(path: "../Record-Presentation"),
        .package(path: "../Record-Pro"),
    ],
    targets: [
        .target(
            name: "Business",
            dependencies: [
                .product(name: "Domain", package: "Record-Foundation"),
                .product(name: "Logging", package: "Record-Foundation"),
            ],
            path: "Sources/Business",
            swiftSettings: sharedSwiftSettings,
        ),
        .executableTarget(
            name: "TheRecord",
            dependencies: [
                "Business",
                .product(name: "Domain", package: "Record-Foundation"),
                .product(name: "Logging", package: "Record-Foundation"),
                .product(name: "Presentation", package: "Record-Presentation"),
                .product(name: "RecordPro", package: "Record-Pro"),
            ],
            path: "Sources/TheRecord",
            swiftSettings: sharedSwiftSettings,
        ),
        .testTarget(
            name: "BusinessTests",
            dependencies: [
                "Business",
                .product(name: "Domain", package: "Record-Foundation"),
            ],
            path: "Tests/Unit/Business",
        ),
        .testTarget(
            name: "InfrastructureTests",
            dependencies: [
                .product(name: "Domain", package: "Record-Foundation"),
            ],
            path: "Tests/Unit/Infrastructure",
            exclude: ["InMemoryCommitmentStoreTests.swift"],
        ),
        .testTarget(
            name: "PresentationTests",
            dependencies: [
                "Business",
                .product(name: "Presentation", package: "Record-Presentation"),
                .product(name: "Domain", package: "Record-Foundation"),
            ],
            path: "Tests/Unit/Presentation",
        ),
    ],
)

Base directory for this skill: /Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/the-record-suite/Record-App/.claude/skills/bodyman-release

# TheRecord Release Builder

## Your Responsibility

Run the release build pipeline and report the DMG path. One script, one output.

---

## Steps

### 0. Check for uncommitted changes

Before building, run:

```bash
wfc git status
```

If there are uncommitted changes, **stop and ask the user** — the DMG SHA is derived from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, so uncommitted work won't be reflected in the build ID. The right question to ask: "You have uncommitted changes — want me to commit them first so they're in the build ID, or release from the current commit?"

Only proceed once the user has confirmed or committed.

### 1. Run the release script

```bash
bash scripts/release.sh --clean --open 2>&1
```

Always pass `--clean`. The script handles everything:
- `swift package clean` — wipes the build cache so no stale artifacts sneak in
- `swift build -c release`
- `.app` bundle assembly with `Info.plist` + entitlements
- Ad-hoc codesigning (uses "TheRecord Dev" identity if present, falls back to `-`)
- DMG creation via `hdiutil`
- Cleanup of DMGs older than the 5 most recent

Other flags:
- `--skip-build` — reuse an existing binary (skip compile + clean), useful for re-signing or re-packaging
- `--open` — open the DMG immediately after creation

### 2. Report the result

When the script succeeds, extract and show the user:
- DMG path (`.build/release/TheRecord-{VERSION}-{SHA}.dmg`)
- DMG size
- One-liner to open it: `open .build/release/TheRecord-*.dmg`

### 3. On failure, diagnose

| Error | Likely cause | Fix |
|-------|-------------|-----|
| `Binary not found` | `swift build -c release` failed | Re-run `swift build -c release 2>&1` and fix compiler errors first |
| `codesign: error` | No signing identity | Acceptable — ad-hoc fallback is used automatically |
| `hdiutil: create failed` | Disk full or bad tmp dir | `df -h .build/` to check space |
| `Permission denied` | Script not executable | `chmod +x scripts/release.sh` |

---

## What NOT to do

- Do not run `swift build` manually before the script — the script does it
- Do not commit the DMG or `.build/` — both are gitignored
- Do not use `xcodebuild` — this is a pure SwiftPM project

skills.content:
Run an adversarial Codex review through the shared plugin runtime.
Position it as a challenge review that questions the chosen implementation, design choices, tradeoffs, and assumptions.
It is not just a stricter pass over implementation defects.

Raw slash-command arguments:
`--scope branch`

Core constraint:
- This command is review-only.
- Do not fix issues, apply patches, or suggest that you are about to make changes.
- Your only job is to run the review and return Codex's output verbatim to the user.
- Keep the framing focused on whether the current approach is the right one, what assumptions it depends on, and where the design could fail under real-world conditions.

Execution mode rules:
- If the raw arguments include `--wait`, do not ask. Run in the foreground.
- If the raw arguments include `--background`, do not ask. Run in a Claude background task.
- Otherwise, estimate the review size before asking:
  - For working-tree review, start with `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.
  - For working-tree review, also inspect both `git diff --shortstat --cached` and `git diff --shortstat`.
  - For base-branch review, use `git diff --shortstat <base>...HEAD`.
  - Treat untracked files or directories as reviewable work for auto or working-tree review even when `git diff --shortstat` is empty.
  - Only conclude there is nothing to review when the relevant scope is actually empty.
  - Recommend waiting only when the scoped review is clearly tiny, roughly 1-2 files total and no sign of a broader directory-sized change.
  - In every other case, including unclear size, recommend background.
  - When in doubt, run the review instead of declaring that there is nothing to review.
- Then use `AskUserQuestion` exactly once with two options, putting the recommended option first and suffixing its label with `(Recommended)`:
  - `Wait for results`
  - `Run in background`

Argument handling:
- Preserve the user's arguments exactly.
- Do not strip `--wait` or `--background` yourself.
- Do not weaken the adversarial framing or rewrite the user's focus text.
- The companion script parses `--wait` and `--background`, but Claude Code's `Bash(..., run_in_background: true)` is what actually detaches the run.
- `/codex:adversarial-review` uses the same review target selection as `/codex:review`.
- It supports working-tree review, branch review, and `--base <ref>`.
- It does not support `--scope staged` or `--scope unstaged`.
- Unlike `/codex:review`, it can still take extra focus text after the flags.

Foreground flow:
- Run:
```bash
node "/Users/samfakhreddine/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/1.0.4/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" adversarial-review "--scope branch"
```
- Return the command stdout verbatim, exactly as-is.
- Do not paraphrase, summarize, or add commentary before or after it.
- Do not fix any issues mentioned in the review output.

Background flow:
- Launch the review with `Bash` in the background:
```typescript
Bash({
  command: `node "/Users/samfakhreddine/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/1.0.4/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" adversarial-review "--scope branch"`,
  description: "Codex adversarial review",
  run_in_background: true
})
```
- Do not call `BashOutput` or wait for completion in this turn.
- After launching the command, tell the user: "Codex adversarial review started in the background. Check `/codex:status` for progress."
